I'm going to wager that many of us don't currently live a simple life, but wish to. I know that my life is full of obligations and things to do, both at work and at home.

So I guess this is a two-fold question:

  1. What is simple living, and
  2. How do we get there from here?

1. I feel like simple living is somewhat personal and different to each person. To me, simple living is working the amount necessary to get the money you need and living the rest of your life in a fulfilling, enjoyable, and positive way.

  2. Since each person has different dreams, goals, and aspirations it is unique and an individualized task. For me, I will need to finish college, work in the career field I have chosen, save enough money to buy a piece of land, build a small house and work part-time for the rest of my life.

I'll answer my own questions:

  1. To me, simple living requires a balance between what you have to do to survive (in my case go to work and earn money to keep a roof over my head) and what you do to enjoy life. I'm fortunate that I work for a company that values work-life balance and sponsors programs that help keep everyone engaged in the culture. It's a very positive place to work. Because of this I have a lot of energy left over to dedicate to things that make me happy, like cooking, and fitness, and other leisure activities.

  2. I have a lot of stress on a regular basis because it feels like I just don't have enough time in the day to do what needs to be done. So perhaps simple living requires better planning; not micromanagement, but planning so you can effectively use your time and build up to your goals in life. Relaxation is key. I personally believe that fitness is important as well (for body and mind).
